issues.observed_problem: The osmosis mechanism is conveyed solely by three static cyan arrows pointing left-to-right across the dashed membrane. The blue water dots and yellow solute squares remain fixed in position throughout 14s–18s; no particle actually crosses the membrane and no concentration gradient visibly shifts over time. A static arrow plus the caption 'Water Follows Solute →' is insufficient to demonstrate a dynamic transport process.
issues.expected_behavior: Animate individual blue water dots translating from the high-water (left) side through the membrane to the low-water (right) side, with the left-side water count decreasing and the right-side water count increasing over several seconds so the viewer observes the net flux as a real-time process.

issues.observed_problem: The three solution-type labels are typeset on the same horizontal line and overlap: at 24s 'Hypotonic → Turgid ✓' and 'Isotonic → Normal =' collide, and at 27s 'Hypertonic → Flaccid ✗' overlaps both. The text is partially illegible, undermining the label dimension and making it difficult for a grade-10–12 viewer to map each solution to its cell state.
issues.expected_behavior: Place the three labels on separate lines or stagger them vertically beneath their respective cells so that 'Hypotonic → Turgid ✓', 'Isotonic → Normal =', and 'Hypertonic → Flaccid ✗' are each fully legible without overlap.

issues.observed_problem: The teaching goal requires showing how water movement across the membrane changes firmness. Section 3 presents three static cell sizes (large/medium/small vacuole) side by side. Only the rightmost cell shows a brief shrinkage animation (25s–27s) with a single outward arrow; the turgid and normal cells never show water entering or leaving over time. The causal link 'water in → firm, water out → soft' is asserted by caption rather than demonstrated as a temporal process for the first two cells.
issues.expected_behavior: For each of the three cells, animate water dots moving across the cell wall/membrane boundary over time (inward for hypotonic, none for isotonic, outward for hypertonic) with the vacuole radius tracking that flux, so the viewer sees firmness change as a consequence of observed water movement.

issues.observed_problem: Static arrows used in place of animated particle motion; no observable change in dot positions over the 4-second window, so the dynamic mechanism is not visually demonstrated.
issues.expected_behavior: Replace or supplement static arrows with animated water-dot trajectories crossing the membrane, showing at least 2–3 seconds of continuous motion.

issues.observed_problem: Overlapping text strings render labels unreadable at 24s and 27s; 'Turgid ✓' and 'Isotonic' merge into a garbled string, and 'Normal =' collides with 'Hypertonic'.
issues.expected_behavior: Reposition labels to non-overlapping vertical positions or use sequential reveal with adequate spacing.
